method: Reviewed official publisher and UPLB repository indexed article text, including the publisher-indexed table descriptions. Direct PDF/page fetches returned HTTP 403, so no local copy was retained and no table, figure or species-by-site matrix was transcribed. Checked the first-party journal/repository reuse policies separately.

surveys.sourceReports: A field survey of three named Makiling Forest Reserve watersheds; the indexed abstract reports site richness of 12, 12 and 9 species, and the indexed Table 1 lists 16 taxa across the three sites.
surveys.dateLimit: The paper's received date is 2010-04-29; no collection date was established from the accessible primary indexed text.
surveys.waterbodyScope: The names match existing Makiling research leads, but this batch does not change their scope assignments.
surveys.taxonomy: Names and native/introduced labels are historical source classifications; no current accepted-name review was completed.
surveys.reuse: PJS describes the journal as open access, while its author guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form. No article-level open reuse license was found. No table or taxa rows are redistributed in this review.
surveys.access: Official PJS indexed text was readable; direct article and PDF requests returned HTTP 403. No local raw copy or visual table review.

surveys.sourceReports: The indexed article reports 1,474 specimens, 15 species, and sampling across upstream, midstream and downstream parts of the river system; identified specimens were sent to the UPLB Museum of Natural History for verification.
surveys.waterbodyScope: The system-level article name may be broader than the existing single Sta Cruz River lead; no assignment or alias was added.
surveys.taxonomy: The article includes a species table, but no rows were transcribed or checked against a current taxonomic authority in this batch.
surveys.reuse: The UKDR policy says authors assign article copyright to UKDR, subject to enumerated personal-use exceptions. No open reuse license for this article was identified. No table or taxa rows are redistributed in this review.
surveys.access: Official UPLB JESAM publisher-indexed text was readable; direct PDF open returned HTTP 403. No local raw copy or visual table review.

rightsPolicySources.title: About PJS
rightsPolicySources.finding: The journal calls itself open access; this page did not establish an item-level reuse license for the 2011 article.

rightsPolicySources.title: PJS Author's Guide
rightsPolicySources.finding: The author guide states that authors sign a copyright-transfer form when a manuscript is accepted.

rightsPolicySources.title: JESAM policies
rightsPolicySources.finding: The policies state that authors assign article copyright to UKDR, with defined personal-use exceptions; they do not grant a third-party public data-reuse license.

limitations: Search-indexed primary article text is not a substitute for a retained, visually reviewed source copy when validating fine-grained table cells.
The Paller survey's collection date is unresolved; the article's publication/received dates are not collection dates.
The Santa Cruz River System's sites may not be equivalent to the scope registry's single Sta Cruz River lead.
Neither study establishes present-day species presence, abundance, catchability, natural diet, safety or fishing legality.
nextAction: Prioritize independently reusable GBIF/OBIS specimen records and rights-cleared government or author-supplied data for these rivers; if the survey tables are needed for public use, request written reuse permission, then visually verify table rows and reconcile every name with current taxonomy before making historical app entries.
